title: Biological Functions of Nuclear O-GalNAc Glycans in Cellular Processes
content: Nuclear post-translational modifications (PTMs) are essential components of biological processes in cell physiology. Glycosylation is the most common PTM in proteins, and various types of O-glycan have been identified in nuclear proteins. However, the functions of nuclear glycosylation of O-GalNAc are still unknown. By implementing multiple experimental approaches in this study we examined selected functional aspects of nuclear O-GalNAc glycosylation in CHO ldlD cells, which lack the capacity to synthesize UDP-Gal and UDP-GalNAc sugar donors. Our results revealed the nuclear localization of ppGalNAc-T3 enzyme, ppGalNAc-transferase activity, the O-GalNAc glycosylation of the key nuclear proteins including Lamin B1, RNA Pol II, EZH2, and histone H3, and the impact of nuclear O-GalNAc glycosylation on intracellular protein levels. This study suggests that nuclear O-GalNAc glycosylation modulates cholesterol biosynthesis and cell proliferation by regulating the transcription of 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA synthase 1. Taken together, these findings suggest that nuclear O-GalNAc glycans play an important role in modulating cellular processes.
